text:
Mike: FYI - microbench shows p95 up ~8% on 4-bit kernels when KV cache hot after kernel-selector change last deploy. Seeing it on x86-gpu pool and on the dedicated c6 nodes.

Devon: Can you paste the perf log / repro command?

Mike: Repro below (quick paste):
```
$ ./run_microbench --model=redwood-4bit --tokens=512 --kv=warm
p50: 23.1ms
p95: 74.2ms  <-- was 68.5ms before
cpu%: 72
gpu_util: 87
kernel: selected q4_v2_fused_attn
fallbacks: int8-matmul on layer 19
kv_hit_latency: +6ms
```

Jess: Interesting — layer 19 fallback on matmul. That layer is in the middle of transformer block: maybe sensitivity to quant calibration. Did we exclude lm_head/emb?

Mike: Yes embeddings + lm_head are excluded in the profile. The fallback is in attention matmul (qk). Calibration table changed shape after FP8 switch PR.

Sara: I think the new kernel selector picks fused_attn when seq_len < 128 else falls back to q4_matmul path. For KV cache warm we have long seqs so selector might mispredict. @Devon can you check the selector heuristics?

Devon: On it. My hunch: selector uses avg_seq_len from recent window (100 samples), but KV cache scenario has prefix 2048 then single tokens — avg skewed. Quick patch: use median or tail-aware metric. I'll try.

BenchBot: CI microbench summary (1795001200): baseline->current: p95 +7.8%, regressions on q4 paths only. Reproducer trace: token=749, layer=19 fallback.

Liam: Also check calibration scale: recent FP8 branch changed per-channel scale dtype — might increase numeric noise for attention qk. If qk matmul triggers fallback due to overflow detection, that's the perf hit.

Jess: Short-term mitigation: pin kernel selector to prefer int8 matmul on layers flagged sensitive + force exclude attention qk from 4-bit for now. Can we ship that as hotfix?

Mike: Agree. I'll open a canary with selector override + added logging: `selector.override_layers=[19,20]; selector.metric=median_seq`. Deploying to dedicated-canary now. (reaction :eyes:)

Devon: Thanks. I'll add a perf test that simulates KV-hot prefix distribution and fail CI if p95 regresses >5%.

Sara: :thumbsup: Also file a short follow-up task to re-evaluate calibration routine — per-layer calibration vs global. We need data on quality impact.

Mike: Filed TASK-4123. Will post results after canary runs.
